heroHeadline: Three Concurrent SCS Flashpoints Persist Post-ASEAN Summit — Reed Bank, Second Thomas Shoal, Scarborough Active Simultaneously; China's CCG Chuanshan Trains at Scarborough Day After Cebu Summit
heroSubtitle: The 48th ASEAN Leaders' Summit (Cebu, May 7-8, 2026) closed with landmark outcomes — the Cebu Protocol (first ASEAN Charter amendment since 2007) and an ASEAN Leaders' Declaration on Maritime Cooperation endorsing an ASEAN Maritime Centre for the Philippines and a permanent ASEAN Coast Guard Forum — but produced no binding South China Sea Code of Conduct, and leaders' renewed call for 'self-restraint' was immediately contradicted by Chinese operational tempo (ASEAN Secretariat, GMA News). On May 9, the day after the summit, China Coast Guard vessel Chuanshan conducted 'comprehensive maritime rights safeguarding and law enforcement training' near Scarborough Shoal (Huangyan Dao) — a deliberate post-summit counter-signal by Beijing demonstrating that diplomatic outcomes in Cebu had no effect on CCG operations in contested waters (China.org.cn). The Philippines simultaneously faces three concurrent active South China Sea confrontations for the first time in the tracker's history: (1) Reed Bank/Iroquois Reef, where China's research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33 continues operations following the May 8 mutual harassment accusations with Philippine Coast Guard Islander aircraft (SCMP); (2) Second Thomas Shoal, where BRP Sierra Madre's ~12-marine garrison continues to require resupply missions under CCG surveillance; and (3) Scarborough Shoal, where the April 2026 floating barrier restricts traditional Philippine fishing grounds and the Chuanshan training continues CCG assertion. Bloomberg reported on May 9 that Vietnam has simultaneously expanded its Spratly Islands outposts by hundreds of acres over the past year — underscoring that multiple claimants are consolidating presence in the absence of a binding COC framework. Exercise Balikatan 2026 formally concluded May 8 after a record 19 days with 17,000+ troops from 7 nations; Defense Secretary Teodoro declared 'credible regional deterrence' at the Camp Aguinaldo closing ceremony, but the three-front SCS confrontation suggests that deterrence posture has not restrained China's gray zone operations in Philippine waters.
